title: A Landowning Housing Society Is Not Automatically Liable for Its Developer's RERA Obligations: Bombay High Court
case_name: Maruthi Co-operative Housing Society v. Tridhaatu Maruthi Developers LLP
card_summary: Justice Arun R. Pedneker gave a Chembur society Section 9 relief to terminate a redevelopment pact and appoint a new developer, after Tridhaatu Maruthi stalled construction, leaving rent and dues unpaid. The court held a landowning society is not liable for the developer's RERA duties merely because the developer sold flats to buyers, and ordered it to clear Rs 7.35 crore in rent and over Rs 1.1 crore in dues.
card_tip: A redevelopment pact should keep RERA registration and promoter duties with the developer; land ownership alone will not make a society liable for the developer's defaults, but still needs a court order to confirm.
verification_notes: Free Press Journal, LiveLawBiz and Mondaq all report the same bench (Justice Arun R. Pedneker), the 16 October 2026 date, the Chembur redevelopment dispute, Tridhaatu's default, and the holding that a landowning society is not automatically liable for the developer's RERA obligations. Figures for unpaid transit rent (Rs 7.35 crore) and statutory dues (reported as Rs 1.10-1.11 crore) are consistent across sources within rounding. The relief is interim and conditional on the society invoking arbitration within a set period; full judgment not independently reviewed.
